subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw own a stable cross-language agent-runtime protocol for non-Node and embedded implementations, beyond its Node-hosted TypeScript runtime and plugin SDK?
rationale: This choice creates a permanent product, compatibility, and security boundary; repository evidence can describe the gap but cannot determine whether OpenClaw should support and maintain that contract.

options.title: Define Narrow Runtime Protocol
options.body: Sponsor a versioned language-neutral agent-loop protocol and conformance suite without committing to porting the full Gateway or every tool.

options.title: Limit Cross-Language Work To Plugins
options.body: Keep OpenClaw Node-hosted and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98004 for non-TypeScript plugin implementations.

options.title: Keep Embedded Ports Independent
options.body: Treat MimiClaw-style projects as external OpenClaw-inspired implementations without an official compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Runtime Protocol
recommendation.body: Sponsor a versioned language-neutral agent-loop protocol and conformance suite without committing to porting the full Gateway or every tool.

likelyOwner.reason: The runtime-internalization history and existing keep-open discussion make this the strongest available owner for the product boundary decision.
